newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA Corp buys more of Argentine pipeline.
newsitem.headline: NOVA Corp buys more of Argentine pipeline.

text.p: NOVA Corp said its NOVA Gas International Ltd unit has purchased 4.7 percent more of Transportadora de Gas del Norte, a 4500-kilometre natural gas pipeline system serving northern Argentina.
NOVA paid about US$30 million for the additional equity, raising its indirect stake in the pipeline system to 19.1 percent from 14.4 percent.

"Argentina plays a central role in natural gas delivery in the Southern Cone of South America, and TGN has exceptional prospects for growth," Gabriel Leon, senior vice president, South America, NOVA Gas International Ltd said in a statement.
When TGN was privatized by the Argentine government in 1992, NOVA and several partners known collectively as Gasinvest S.A. bought a 70 percent stake in the pipeline.
One of the original Gasinvest partners -- a group of Argentine and international financial investors -- has now sold its 13.9 per cent stake in TGN to NOVA and the remaining Gasinvest partners.
The other 30 per cent interest in TGN is held by CMS Energy of Dearborn, Michigan, and TGN's employees.
TGN's current delivery capacity is roughly 32 million cubic metres (1.13 billion cubic feet) a day.
TGN expects to invest more than US$300 million over the next three years to expand its system to meet growing domestic and regional demand for natural gas, NOVA said.
